title: Northbridge — Security review (SOC 2, audit logs, SSO, retention)
summary: Northbridge security review focused on Redwood Inference Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private responsibilities, SOC 2 scope and evidence access, audit logging coverage and export, data retention/deletion behavior, incident notification language, and SSO/SAML/SCIM and RBAC. Redwood agreed to send the updated Enterprise Security FAQ v2 and the one-pager pack; GRC to initiate SOC 2 report sharing flow under NDA and provide pen test summary process. Follow-up scheduled to confirm retention defaults for their intended deployment mode and review audit log events for SIEM mapping.

Audit logs: events, coverage, export/SIEM options, differences by deployment mode
Data retention + deletion requests; logs vs prompts/outputs
SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles and least-privilege
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private shared responsibility

Olga (GRC) to share SOC 2 report access instructions and confirm NDA requirements; provide pen test summary availability under NDA.
Northbridge to confirm target deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and preferred region so Redwood can answer retention/residency precisely.
Schedule 30-min follow-up with Northbridge Security + IT to walk through SAML/SCIM setup and audit log export to their SIEM.

transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcription

Meeting: Northbridge — Security review (SOC 2, audit logs, SSO, retention)
Date: 2026-01-22
Start time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 46 min

Attendees
- Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood Inference, AE)
- Simran Kaur (Redwood Inference, Solutions Architect)
- Olga Petrov (Redwood Inference, GRC/Compliance)
- Priya Desai (Northbridge, Security)
- Matt Reynolds (Northbridge, IT / IAM)
- Jon Park (Northbridge, Engineering)

Auto-summary (generated)
- Customer is evaluating Redwood for LLM inference for internal knowledge assistant + customer support drafts.
- Key blockers: SOC 2 scope, audit log availability/export, data retention defaults, incident notification language, SSO/SAML and SCIM.
- Redwood to provide updated Security FAQ v2 and one-pagers; SOC 2 report shared under NDA.


Transcript

[00:00] Stephanie Nguyen: Cool, okay. Um, thanks everybody for making time. This is our security review slot for Northbridge. I’m Stephanie, account exec on the Redwood side. Simran is our solutions architect, and Olga joined from compliance. 

[00:12] Priya Desai: Hi, Priya here, security. 

[00:14] Matt Reynolds: Matt, I run IAM and SSO stuff. 

[00:16] Jon Park: Jon, engineering. 

[00:18] Stephanie Nguyen: Great. The goal today is to get through your top questions and then we’ll follow up with the right docs. I know you asked for SOC 2, audit logging, retention, incident notifications, and SSO. 

[00:32] Priya Desai: Yep. And just to level set, we’re mid procurement. We need to clear internal security review before we can sign anything.

[00:40] Stephanie Nguyen: Understood. Maybe starting point—can you confirm which deployment mode you’re considering? Hosted API versus Dedicated capacity versus Private in your VPC.

[00:50] Jon Park: Right now we’re thinking Hosted for speed, but our security team is… skeptical. Dedicated might be okay. VPC maybe later.

[01:00] Priya Desai: We have some regulated customers so data handling matters. We’re not saying “must be on prem” but we need a clear story.

[01:08] Simran Kaur: Makes sense. We’ll be careful to separate what’s true for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private because the boundaries do change.

[01:18] Stephanie Nguyen: Cool. Priya, do you want to start with SOC 2?

[01:22] Priya Desai: Yes. Are you SOC 2 Type II? What’s in scope? And can you share the report?

[01:30] Olga Petrov: Yeah. We maintain a SOC 2 Type II report. Scope includes the production systems supporting the Redwood hosted inference platform and associated corporate controls, and the trust services criteria are Security and Availability. Exact system description and boundaries are in the report.

[01:48] Priya Desai: Is Dedicated in scope?

[01:51] Olga Petrov: Dedicated as a service offering uses the same control framework and operational processes; whether a specific customer’s dedicated environment is explicitly described depends on the system boundary section. We can point you to the relevant language in the report and the bridge letter if applicable. I don’t want to paraphrase too aggressively on a call.

[02:10] Priya Desai: Okay. Can you just email it?

[02:12] Olga Petrov: We can share under NDA. Usually we either confirm you have an NDA with Redwood or we put one in place, then we distribute via an approved process and track recipients. Turnaround is typically one to two business days once NDA is confirmed.

[02:28] Stephanie Nguyen: We can start that today after the call.

[02:31] Priya Desai: Fine. Next: audit logs. What events do you log and can we export to our SIEM?

[02:39] Simran Kaur: Sure. At a high level, there are a few categories: identity/admin events in the Console (like login, SSO changes, API key creation/rotation), organization/project changes, and some API usage and operational telemetry. The exact event names are in our audit logging overview one-pager—because the names in the UI can be a little specific.

[03:03] Matt Reynolds: Do you log the prompts? Like the text we send.

[03:08] Simran Kaur: Good question. We separate “audit logs” from “request/response payload logging.” Audit logs are about actions and access and configuration. For payloads, defaults depend on deployment mode and the features enabled. We can walk through the retention one-pager because it gets nuanced—like standard service logs vs customer content.

[03:28] Priya Desai: We need something definitive, not “nuanced.”

[03:31] Stephanie Nguyen: Totally fair. We have an updated retention controls one-pager that states defaults and what can be configured. It also calls out differences between Hosted and Dedicated, and what changes in Private.

[03:43] Priya Desai: Export—how do we get the audit logs out?

[03:46] Simran Kaur: Today, customers can access audit logs in the Redwood Console for the org. For exports, we support retrieval via API, and for some enterprise setups we can route to customer storage or integrate into SIEM pipelines—depending on mode. I’m being careful: I don’t want to promise a specific connector if you mean “native Splunk app.”

[04:10] Matt Reynolds: Yeah we’re on Splunk.

[04:12] Simran Kaur: Got it. Most teams do API pull and forward into Splunk, or use an internal log forwarder. We can provide sample events so you can map fields. 

[04:24] Priya Desai: Do you have like… tamper-proof logs? Immutable?

[04:29] Simran Kaur: In Hosted, the logs are managed in our control plane and access is RBAC controlled; we maintain integrity controls around logging as part of our security program. If you need immutability on your side, exporting into your own WORM/immutable bucket is typically how teams satisfy that.

[04:48] Olga Petrov: And SOC 2 covers controls around logging and monitoring, but again, specifics are in the report.

[04:56] Priya Desai: Okay. Retention. What do you retain by default for customer data, and for how long?

[05:05] Stephanie Nguyen: Before we answer, can I ask: are you planning to send any regulated data through prompts? Like PHI, PCI, that sort of thing.

[05:12] Jon Park: Not PHI. Potentially internal customer notes, but we can redact. The biggest concern is “are our prompts stored” and “for how long.”

[05:24] Simran Kaur: Right. In Hosted, there are a couple layers: (1) transient processing in memory for inference, (2) service logs/metrics, and (3) optional features like request logging for debugging. Our default posture is to minimize retention of customer content, and we provide controls and documented retention periods. The one-pager spells out retention defaults and how deletion requests work.

[05:50] Priya Desai: I’m going to push. “Minimize” is not a number.

[05:54] Olga Petrov: The one-pager includes specific timeframes for categories: operational logs, audit logs, and any customer-content logging if enabled. Some settings are configurable on enterprise plans. I’d rather send the exact language than risk a mismatch in transcription.

[06:12] Matt Reynolds: Are audit logs retained longer than other logs?

[06:15] Simran Kaur: Often yes, because audit logs are for security and compliance review, but we also support configuring retention in certain cases. Again it varies with Hosted vs Dedicated.

[06:28] Priya Desai: Deletion requests—how do those work?

[06:31] Stephanie Nguyen: There’s a documented process via support and your CSM/TAM, and the retention one-pager covers it at a customer-facing level. We can also include the contact for security inquiries.

[06:44] Priya Desai: Okay. Incident notification. What’s your commitment? 24 hours, 72 hours?

[06:52] Olga Petrov: We have an incident response program and customer notification approach. Specific notification timelines are contract dependent—set in the MSA and any security addendum. We avoid “always 24” blanket statements because different customers negotiate different terms and the definition of “security incident” matters.

[07:14] Priya Desai: We usually require 72 hours for confirmed breach impacting our data.

[07:18] Stephanie Nguyen: That’s common. We can work with legal on the exact language when you get to paper.

[07:23] Jon Park: How do you notify? Email? Portal?

[07:26] Simran Kaur: For incidents impacting service availability, we post to our status page. For security incidents involving customer data, it’s typically direct communication to the customer’s designated contacts, plus ongoing updates as we learn more.

[07:43] Priya Desai: Do you have a public status page?

[07:45] Simran Kaur: Yes. We’ll send the link. 

[07:49] Matt Reynolds: Okay SSO. You support SAML?

[07:52] Simran Kaur: Yes—SAML 2.0 for SSO into the Redwood Console. We support common IdPs like Okta, Azure AD, Ping. The setup is typically metadata exchange. 

[08:08] Matt Reynolds: And SCIM? For provisioning.

[08:11] Simran Kaur: SCIM is available for enterprise plans for user provisioning and deprovisioning. The one-pager covers recommended patterns: enforce SSO, disable local password login, and use SCIM to manage group membership where possible.

[08:28] Priya Desai: Do you have RBAC or is it like “admin or not admin.”

[08:33] Simran Kaur: RBAC, yes. There are roles at org and project levels. We can share the RBAC model reference which has a matrix of permissions. Most customers use least privilege: separate billing admin from security admin from developer. 

[08:53] Jon Park: Does RBAC apply to API keys too?

[08:56] Simran Kaur: API keys are scoped, yes—project-level keys, and actions like key creation/rotation are logged in audit logs.

[09:06] Priya Desai: Good. What about MFA?

[09:10] Matt Reynolds: If we do SSO we handle MFA in Okta.

[09:12] Simran Kaur: Exactly—when SSO is enforced, MFA is via your IdP policy. For non-SSO users (if allowed), we have additional controls, but enterprise recommendation is enforce SSO.

[09:25] Stephanie Nguyen: Priya, anything else on identity?

[09:28] Priya Desai: Encryption. At rest and in transit.

[09:31] Simran Kaur: In transit is TLS. At rest, data is encrypted. For key management, in Hosted we manage keys; in Dedicated there are options to integrate with customer-managed keys depending on architecture, and for Private in your VPC you can use your own KMS/HSM because you operate the environment. That’s in the encryption and key management one-pager.

[09:57] Priya Desai: Okay. Data residency: can we guarantee US-only processing?

[10:03] Stephanie Nguyen: We have region selection and residency guidance. For Hosted, you can choose the region where inference is served from, subject to availability. For Dedicated and Private, you can pin to specific regions/VPCs. We’ll send the data residency one-pager because it also covers logs/telemetry and what’s regional vs global.

[10:26] Priya Desai: We’ve been burned on “US region” but then support logs go elsewhere.

[10:31] Simran Kaur: That’s exactly why the one-pager calls out telemetry and support access patterns. In general, we limit access and follow least privilege, and can support additional controls for regulated workloads. But specifics depend on contract and deployment.

[10:50] Jon Park: For Dedicated, is it single tenant GPU?

[10:53] Stephanie Nguyen: Dedicated is reserved capacity and isolated at the infrastructure level—single-tenant resource allocation. The exact implementation details we can discuss, but it’s meant for predictable throughput and data isolation.

[11:09] Priya Desai: Do you do pen tests?

[11:11] Olga Petrov: Yes. We have independent security assessments. We can share an executive summary under NDA, and we can answer questionnaires with evidence pointers.

[11:24] Priya Desai: Vulnerability management? Patch SLAs?

[11:27] Simran Kaur: We have a secure SDLC and vulnerability remediation process with severity-based SLAs. There’s a customer-facing SDLC summary one-pager as well.

[11:42] Priya Desai: Ok. I’m going to list what I need to close this: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, audit logs details with export, retention statement in writing, incident notification language, and SSO/SCIM confirmation.

[12:00] Stephanie Nguyen: Yep. We have a packaged kit that includes (1) Enterprise Security FAQ v2, and (2) one-pagers for audit logging, retention controls, residency, SSO/SAML/SCIM and RBAC, incident response, and secure SDLC. The SOC 2 and pen test summary are via the evidence sharing process Olga mentioned.

[12:22] Priya Desai: Great. Is the FAQ current? We got something last year that was… out of date.

[12:27] Stephanie Nguyen: Yes, this is the refreshed v2. It has a “last reviewed” stamp and it’s aligned across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

[12:38] Matt Reynolds: Quick technical question. Audit log—does it include “model change” events? Like if someone changes a model version.

[12:45] Simran Kaur: Yes, configuration changes like model routing policies and key admin actions are in audit logs. I’m going to double-check the exact event label so we don’t misstate it. I’ll send sample event categories.

[13:00] Jon Park: Can we get streaming logs? Like real-time?

[13:03] Simran Kaur: Real-time streaming depends on your export mechanism. If you pull frequently via API you can get near real-time. Some customers want a push-based integration; we’ll clarify what’s available today versus what’s on roadmap, but we won’t put roadmap in security answers unless it’s clearly labeled.

[13:23] Priya Desai: Thanks for saying that. We do not accept “roadmap” as a control.

[13:27] Stephanie Nguyen: Totally aligned.

[13:30] (cross talk)

[13:31] Matt Reynolds: Sorry—SSO setup. Is it per org? Per project?

[13:34] Simran Kaur: SSO enforcement is at the org level for Console access. Projects inherit that. API access is via keys/tokens and governed by RBAC and key management.

[13:48] Priya Desai: Alright. Can you send everything today?

[13:51] Stephanie Nguyen: I can send the FAQ PDF and one-pagers today. For SOC 2 report, we’ll start NDA confirmation and then share via the approved path—likely tomorrow.

[14:03] Olga Petrov: I’ll email you the SOC 2 access instructions right after this. If you already have an NDA in place, we can move quickly.

[14:11] Priya Desai: We have one with Redwood from a prior evaluation. I’ll check if it’s still active.

[14:18] Stephanie Nguyen: Perfect.

[14:20] Jon Park: While we have you—if we go Dedicated, can we control retention more strictly?

[14:25] Simran Kaur: Typically yes, because the environment is more isolated and we can offer more configuration knobs. Private is where you have the most control, because it’s in your network boundary. But let’s map it to your requirements. 

[14:43] Priya Desai: We’re not ready for VPC/on prem yet.

[14:46] Stephanie Nguyen: Understood.

[14:48] Priya Desai: Any subprocessor list? DPA?

[14:52] Olga Petrov: Yes, we maintain a subprocessor list and can provide it. DPA is handled through legal; we can get you the standard template and any addendum process.

[15:06] Priya Desai: Okay.

[15:08] Stephanie Nguyen: We’re about 15 minutes in—do you want to keep drilling in on any one area? Or should we confirm next steps and follow up with docs?

[15:17] Priya Desai: Let’s do a little more on incident response. How do you define incident vs breach?

[15:23] Olga Petrov: Generally, a security incident is a broader category—suspected or confirmed events that may affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability. A breach typically refers to confirmed unauthorized access or disclosure of customer data. But the contract definitions govern, so we typically point to the security addendum language rather than inventing a definition on a call.

[15:45] Priya Desai: Good.

[15:46] Matt Reynolds: Do you have a security contact email?

[15:49] Stephanie Nguyen: Yes, there’s a security contact in the FAQ and we’ll include it.

[15:54] Jon Park: How do you handle support access? Like if we open a ticket, does someone access our data?

[16:01] Simran Kaur: Support access is controlled and logged. Typically, we use least privilege and need-to-know. We can also support customer-controlled access patterns in enterprise scenarios. Again, specifics are in the security FAQ and the residency/retention docs because it’s connected.

[16:22] Priya Desai: Alright. I think we’re good.

[16:25] Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Let me recap what we’ll send:

[16:28] Stephanie Nguyen: One: the updated Enterprise Security FAQ v2. Two: one-pagers—Audit Logging Overview, Data Retention Controls, Data Residency, SSO/SAML/SCIM and RBAC, Incident Response and Notification, and Secure SDLC Summary. Three: Olga will kick off SOC 2 report sharing under NDA and provide pen test summary availability.

[16:55] Priya Desai: Yes.

[16:56] Stephanie Nguyen: And then we should schedule a short follow-up for Matt and Simran to go through SAML and SCIM and audit log export mapping to Splunk.

[17:05] Matt Reynolds: Works.

[17:06] Jon Park: Works.

[17:07] Priya Desai: Okay.

[17:09] Stephanie Nguyen: Cool. Any final questions before we drop?

[17:13] Priya Desai: No. Just please make sure it’s the latest versions, not old docs.

[17:18] Stephanie Nguyen: Yep, we’ll include version stamps and “last reviewed.”

[17:23] Olga Petrov: And I’ll note what is customer-shareable versus restricted evidence.

[17:28] Stephanie Nguyen: Great. Thanks everyone.

[17:31] (meeting ends)

Note: Transcript auto-ended early due to silence detection; call continued briefly offline per participants.
